name: Mr. Cake Resumes Work on the Clock
description: In the overgrown silence of an old New Orleans cemetery, where vines curl over weathered sepulchers, Mr. Cake returns to his task. He bends over the clock, hands moving with quiet precision, adjusting gears and tightening springs. The air hums faintly as the mechanism begins to stir, responding to his touch.
related_events: Mr. Cake resumes working on his clock

name: Parents See Son Off at the Train Station
description: The parents stood on the platform of the old train station, their son beside them with a bag in hand. He boarded the train, turned, and waved through the window. They raised their hands in silence as the train pulled away, steam rising into the air.
related_events: Son departs for the army from the old train station

name: Daisy's Quiet Smile
description: A faint smile appears on Daisy's lips as she quietly murmurs 'Mr. Cake' to herself.
related_events: Daisy forms a slight smile and silently repeats 'Mr. Cake'

name: Mr. Gateau Completes the Clock
description: Mr. Gateau carefully sets the last spring into place and secures the back of the clock. The device is now fully assembled.
related_events: Mr. Gateau finishes assembling the clock

name: Martin Returns to His Parents
description: Martin hops backward off the train and lands where his journey began. His parents are waiting, and they embrace him.
related_events: Martin hops backward off the train to reunite with his parents

name: Thomas Carries Crying Baby Through Crowded Streets
description: Thomas walks through crowded streets, tears streaming down his face, as he carries his crying baby. He pushes through the dense crowd, moving urgently forward.
related_events: Thomas carries crying baby through crowded streets

name: Man Rushes Past Maid and Bursts into Master Bedroom
description: He runs past a solemn maid up a long staircase and barges into the master bedroom.
related_events: He runs past a solemn maid up a long staircase
He barges into the master bedroom

name: Thomas Flees with the Crying Infant
description: Thomas hurried through narrow streets, the wail of the infant in his arms echoing against the crumbling walls of old antebellum houses. He passed dim back porches and sagging stairs, moving quickly between the shadowed sides of buildings, his steps urgent, the child clinging to him as they went.
related_events: Thomas carries crying infant through narrow streets

name: Daisy Helps Mr. Cake to Bed
description: After the clocks strike midnight, a Creole woman named Daisy enters Mr. Cake's workshop. She takes his arm and helps him rise from his work. Guiding him gently, she leads him upstairs and shows him to his bed.
related_events: Creole woman enters Mr. Cake's workshop at midnight
Creole woman assists Mr. Cake to his bed

name: Teddy Roosevelt Removes His Hat, Monsieur Gateau Speaks of His Son
description: Teddy Roosevelt stands quietly and removes his hat. Monsieur Gateau looks ahead and says that perhaps his own son might come home again.
related_events: Teddy Roosevelt removes his hat in grief
Monsieur Gateau expresses hope for his son's return

name: Mr. Cake and His Wife Attend the Gateau Family Burial
description: Mr. Cake, wearing his familiar hat, stands with his wife at his side, both of them among the mourners gathered in the Gateau family burial ground. Rows of coffins line the space around them as the ceremony unfolds. They remain still, part of the quiet assembly observing the burial rites.
related_events: Mr. Cake and his wife stand among rows of coffins during a burial

name: Mr. Gateau Waves Goodbye to His Son
description: The Gateau family stands together at the train station as their son boards a flatbed train filled with soldiers. He hugs his parents before climbing onto the train. The engine starts, and the train begins to move. Mr. Gateau lifts his hat and waves it steadily as the train pulls away, his eyes fixed on his son until the distance blurs the figure.
related_events: Mr. Gateau waves goodbye to his son
Son departs on flatbed train with soldiers
related_occasions: Departure Of Soldiers From The Train Station

name: The Doctor Finishes His Examination
description: The Doctor closed his medical bag after finishing the examination of an elderly boarder. He stood quietly for a moment, then Queenie stepped beside him and spoke.
related_events: Doctor completes examination of elderly boarder
Doctor packs medical bag
Queenie approaches and speaks to the Doctor

name: Daisy's Voiceover Introduces Mr. Gateau's Clock Shop
description: The camera moves over an old storefront in the French Quarter, its windows crowded with clocks and watches of all sizes. Gears turn, pendulums swing, and hands tick forward in silent rhythm. Inside, the faint sound of ticking fills the air. A voice, Daisy's, speaks softly. She says the man who owns this place is named Mr. Gateau. Mr. Cake.
related_events: Camera reveals old French Quarter storefront filled with clocks and watches

name: The Clock Unveiling at the New Train Station
description: A tuba band plays oom-pah-pah music on the steps of the new train station as a ribbon is cut. Amid the celebration, the clock built by the finest clockmaker in the South is unveiled for the first time, its face gleaming in the sunlight.
related_events: finest clockmaker's clock is unveiled at train station
tuba band performs during ribbon cutting ceremony
related_occasions: Ribbon Cutting Ceremony At New Train Station

name: Cymbals Close the Music at Sybil Wagner's Funeral
description: At an old cemetery, a crank Victrola plays 'Die Valkyrie' during Sybil Wagner's funeral. As the music winds down, an old man steps forward and strikes a pair of cymbals, the sharp sound ringing out as a final musical note over the gravesite.
related_events: Playback of 'Die Valkyrie' during funeral
Old man performs cymbal bang as musical finale

name: General Winslow Raises the Flag Naked in the Rain
description: General Winslow stands in the pouring rain, raising the flag barefoot and completely naked. Queenie runs across the wet lawn, clutching a coat in her arms, heading toward him. As she moves, the sound of opera fills the air, sung by Mrs. Sybil Wagner, whose voice carries through the downpour.
related_events: General Winslow raises flag in downpour while naked
Queenie runs across lawn to bring coat to General Winslow
Mrs. Sybil Wagner sings opera during the flag-raising

name: General Winslow Leaves His Birthday Celebration
description: A cake is brought into the room, lit with candles, as part of General Winslow's birthday gathering. He looks at it silently, then stands, mutters something under his breath, and walks out. The other guests, mostly elderly, watch him go. Without speaking, they turn back to the table, pick up forks, and begin eating the cake.
related_events: General Winslow leaves his birthday celebration
Attendees eat cake after General Winslow's departure

name: Morning Rituals at the Residence
description: The Victrola plays music as Mrs. Wagner stands at the window in her nightgown, singing loudly along with the record. Down the hall, Queenie bathes Benjamin and gently massages his legs, working to loosen their stiffness. At exactly six o'clock, breakfast is served.
related_events: Queenie gives Benjamin a bath and massages his legs
Mrs. Wagner sings with Victrola music at window
Breakfast is served at six o'clock

name: Benjamin Watches the Sunset with the Elderly Residents
description: Benjamin sits on the nursing home porch in his wheelchair alongside the elderly residents as the sun sets. The air is still, the light soft at the end of the day. They watch in silence, their faces calm, each absorbed in the quiet moment. One of them passes gas, the sound breaking gently into the stillness. No one reacts. The sky deepens in color, and the warmth of the fading light rests on their skin.
related_events: Elderly resident passes gas on the porch
Benjamin Button reflects on growing up among elderly residents
related_occasions: Evening Gathering On The Nursing Home Porch

name: Thomas Button Arrives at the Town Home Amid Fireworks Celebration
description: Fireworks burst in the night sky over New Orleans, lighting the streets as crowds of revelers shout, sing, and embrace in celebration of the war's end. Cars clog the cobblestone roads, and the air hums with noise and motion. Thomas Button, a man in his early 30s, runs through the chaos toward a fashionable town home. He reaches the gate just as a priest arrives at the same time. They nearly collide, but Thomas pushes past, hurrying up the steps without stopping.
related_events: Fireworks explosion marks the end of World War I celebration in New Orleans
Thomas Button arrives at the town home during the celebration
Thomas Button nearly collides with a priest at the town home gate

name: Mr. Oti Stops the Streetcar
description: Mr. Oti suddenly runs into the street and dashes in front of an oncoming streetcar, waving his arms. The streetcar screeches to a halt. Benjamin, moving as fast as he can, struggles to catch up behind him.
related_events: Mr. Oti runs into the street and stops a streetcar
Benjamin attempts to keep up with Mr. Oti

name: Children Stare as Benjamin and Mr. Oti Enter the Street
description: Benjamin and Mr. Oti step out onto the street. The children playing there come to a sudden stop, turning to stare in silence. Their eyes fix on Benjamin, then shift to Mr. Oti, who suddenly darts into the road. Mr. Oti waves his arms frantically at an approaching streetcar, forcing it to halt with a screech of brakes.
related_events: Children stop playing and stare at Benjamin and Mr. Oti

name: Bullets Return to Rifles, the Fallen Rise
description: Bullets pull from wounds and streak back into rifles. Limbs torn apart reattach, whole and unbroken. Cannonballs reverse their paths, soaring from craters into the muzzles of cannons. Soldiers who lay still on the battlefield rise to their feet, breathing, moving, alive once more.
related_events: Bullets retract from wounds into rifles
Limbs regenerate to wholeness
Cannonballs fly backward into cannons
Fallen soldiers rise and regain life

name: Monsieur Gateau Describes Survivors Returning Home
description: Bullets pull free from wounds, flying back into rifles. Limbs reattach, whole and unbroken. Cannonballs reverse through the air, vanishing into the muzzles of cannons. The fallen rise, breathing, standing, alive. Monsieur Gateau speaks of men and women returning to their homes, tending fields, working at their trades, gathering with families. Children laugh in the distance. Life moves forward, quiet and full.
related_events: Monsieur Gateau describes return to civilian life

name: Tizzy Teaches Benjamin to Read and Count in the Kitchen
description: Benjamin sits in his wheelchair in the kitchen, working with Tizzy as she guides him through reading the word on the page. He sounds out 'bis' and then 'graby,' and Tizzy corrects him gently, pointing to the letter 'v.' He tries again and says 'gravy.' She smiles and praises him. She then asks how many parts of butter they have, and he answers four. When asked about flour, he says two. She presses him to add the two amounts, and he says six. Tizzy smacks the back of his head playfully. A group of staff enters, picking up platters of food as Benjamin finishes his answers. Dinner is served promptly at six.
related_events: Benjamin learns to read under Tizzy's guidance
Benjamin answers arithmetic question during cooking lesson
Tizzy physically reacts to Benjamin's correct answer
related_occasions: Cooking And Reading Lesson With Tizzy And Benjamin

name: Serving Dinner After the Lesson
description: Benjamin sits in his wheelchair in the kitchen, still going over words with Tizzy. He reads aloud, sounding out 'biscuits and gravy' as Tizzy corrects his pronunciation. Staff members enter, carrying large platters of food, moving with purpose. Tizzy quizzes Benjamin on measurements—how many parts butter, how many parts flour, how much together. Benjamin answers correctly, and Tizzy gives him a light smack on the back of the head in approval. Inside the dining area, dinner is served exactly at six. Benjamin Button’s voice speaks over the scene, calm and steady: 'Dinner was served promptly at six.'
related_events: Staff enter kitchen with food platters
Dinner is served at six o'clock
related_occasions: Cooking And Reading Lesson With Tizzy And Benjamin

name: Benjamin Listens to the Sleeping House
description: An old woman sits asleep in an easy chair, a book resting on her lap. Benjamin sits in his wheelchair, still and quiet, listening to the sounds of the house. The creak of wood, the faint breath of those sleeping. He remains in the stillness, watching, hearing, present in the calm. Outside, the world is dark, the streetlights glowing beyond the gate. Inside, the house breathes around him.
related_events: Benjamin listens to the sounds of the sleeping house
Old Woman falls asleep in easy chair with book on lap

name: Benjamin Looks Beyond the Gate
description: Benjamin wheels himself to the window and sits looking outside. The streetlights glow along the road, and beyond the gate, the world lies quiet and still. He watches, taking in the night beyond the house.
related_events: Benjamin wheels himself to the window to look outside

name: General Winslow Raises the Flag at Dawn
description: Every morning at 5:30, no matter the weather, General Winslow, retired from the U.S. Army, steps outside and raises the flag. The routine never varies. From his wheelchair, Benjamin watches through the window, listening to the familiar sounds of the house and the quiet movements of the neighborhood waking. Outside, the streetlights still glow as the general completes his ritual, the flag rising steadily into the early sky.
related_events: General Winslow raises the flag every morning at 5:30

name: Monsieur Gateau Presents His Clock and Leaves
description: Monsieur Gateau says he is sorry if he has offended anyone and invites the onlookers to enjoy his clock. His wife takes his arm, and together they walk across the terminal and exit. The crowd remains still, watching in silence. Teddy Roosevelt puts on his hat and departs with his guardians. Monsieur Gateau is never seen again.
related_events: Monsieur Gateau apologizes and presents his clock
Monsieur Gateau exits the terminal with his wife

name: The Crowd Waits in Silence
description: After Monsieur Gateau exited the terminal with his wife holding his arm, the crowd stood still. They turned toward Teddy Roosevelt, waiting. Without speaking, he placed his hat on his head and walked away, accompanied by his guardians. No one followed. No one spoke. The terminal remained quiet.
related_events: Crowd remains motionless seeking guidance
Teddy Roosevelt puts on his hat and departs with guardians

name: Monsieur Gateau Disappears Amid Rumors
description: Monsieur Gateau leaves the terminal with his wife, his arm held tightly as they walk through the crowd. The onlookers stand still, turning to Teddy Roosevelt for a sign, but he only places his hat on his head and departs with his guardians. Monsieur Gateau is never seen again. Some say he died of a broken heart. Others say he went to sea.
related_events: Monsieur Gateau disappears and rumors spread about his fate

name: Blanche Delivers the Death Letter
description: Blanche Devereux enters Mr. Gateau's workshop holding a letter. The sound of clocks ticking fills the room. She approaches her blind husband and reads the letter aloud. It informs them that their son, Sgt. Martin Gateau, was killed in the Battle of the Marne. The letter expresses sorrow from his commanding officer and comrades, and mentions that his personal belongings—his pants, shirt, cavalry pin, kerchief, and haircomb—are being sent. After reading, she remains with him as he sits in silence. Later, Mr. Gateau rises and slowly makes his way up the stairs to bed, feeling each step with his hands.
related_events: Blanche Devereux enters Mr. Gateau's workshop with a letter
Blanche reads the death notification letter to her blind husband
Mr. Gateau receives personal effects of his deceased son

name: Mr. Gateau Goes to Bed After Learning of His Son's Death
description: After Blanche reads the letter informing them of their son Martin's death at the Battle of the Marne, Mr. Gateau remains silent in his workshop. He finishes his work as the clocks tick around him. Then, feeling his way along the walls, he ascends the stairs and goes to bed.
related_events: Mr. Gateau goes to bed after finishing his work for the night

name: Sgt. Martin Gateau Comes Home
description: The sound of clocks ticking fills the workshop as Mr. Gateau works, then slowly makes his way upstairs, feeling each step with his hands. Blanche enters, holding a letter. She reads aloud to her blind husband: their son, Sgt. Martin Gateau, has been killed in the Battle of the Marne. The letter speaks of sorrow among his comrades, of lost hopes for his return, and mentions the personal items being sent back—his pants, shirt, cavalry pin, kerchief, and haircomb. Mr. Gateau ascends to bed in silence. And then, in the stillness, their son comes home.

name: Caroline Examines the Journal
description: Caroline sits with the journal on her knees, flipping through its pages. She pauses, noticing several pages have been torn out. As she continues to look inside, she finds an old streetcar token tucked within the binding. She picks it up, studies it for a moment, then places it in her mother’s hand, closing Daisy’s fingers around it. Daisy does not respond, her eyes closed, her gaze fixed on the window. Caroline watches her, then looks back at the journal, her expression uncertain.
related_events: Caroline questions the truth of the journal's contents
Caroline notices pages are missing from the journal
Caroline finds an old streetcar token inside the journal

name: Caroline Gives Daisy the Streetcar Token
description: Caroline finds an old streetcar token inside the journal and places it in her mother's hand, closing Daisy's fingers around it. Daisy does not respond, her eyes fixed on the window. The wind knocks against the glass. She murmurs about a clock that kept going, year after year, without looking at her daughter.
related_events: Caroline gives the streetcar token to her mother
Daisy becomes lost in thought while looking out the window

name: Daisy Compliments Caroline's Voice
description: Caroline holds the journal on her knees and asks if any of it is true. Daisy closes her eyes and says, 'You have such a lovely voice.' Caroline shrugs and continues looking through the book, noticing that some pages are torn out. Inside, she finds an old streetcar token and places it in her mother's hand, folding Daisy's fingers around it. Daisy does not respond, her gaze fixed out the window as she murmurs, 'That clock... Just kept going, year after year after year...'
related_events: Daisy compliments Caroline's voice

name: Queenie Hides the Baby Under the Stairs
description: Queenie moves quietly down a hallway, cradling a crying baby, her steps careful and deliberate. Tizzy follows close behind, whispering in a hushed and anxious tone. From somewhere out of sight, a woman’s voice calls out, 'Where are you, Queenie?' Queenie snaps back, 'Hold your water,' then turns to Tizzy and tells him to go tend to the others. He turns and walks away without a word. Alone now, Queenie hurries to a small room tucked beneath the stairs, slips inside, and places the baby there.
related_events: Queenie sneaks through hallway carrying crying baby
Tizzy follows Queenie while whispering anxiously
Unseen woman calls out to Queenie
Queenie silences caller and sends Tizzy away
Queenie hides baby in small room under stairs
related_occasions: Gathering At The Old Age Home

name: Piano Music and Singing in the Parlor
description: In the parlor of the old age home, a piano plays a familiar tune. The residents, seated among heavy furniture and worn carpets, join in singing along. Their voices rise together, soft and uneven, filling the dim room. The music continues as Queenie moves quietly down the hallway with a crying baby, slipping away from the gathering, while Tizzy lingers nearby before being sent off by her to attend to someone calling her name.
related_events: Piano performance accompanied by singing in parlor
related_occasions: Gathering At The Old Age Home

name: Benjamin's Wheelchair Disruption on the Porch
description: Benjamin, seated in his wheelchair among the elderly residents on the porch, begins moving back and forth between them, breaking the steady rhythm of their rocking. The repeated motion draws the attention of one of the old men, who finally extends his cane into the spokes of Benjamin's wheelchair, bringing it to an abrupt halt. The porch falls back into its usual cadence as Benjamin sits still among the others.
related_events: Benjamin wheels his chair back and forth among the old people
Old man stops Benjamin's wheelchair with his cane

name: Benjamin Watches the Rocking Elders
description: After the old man stops Benjamin's wheelchair with his cane, Benjamin sits among the elderly on the porch. He remains still as the old people continue to rock back and forth in their chairs. Around him, the rhythmic creaking of rockers fills the air. From beyond the wall, the sounds of children playing and carriages arriving drift in, mingling with the quiet of the porch.
related_events: Benjamin sits and observes the old people rocking on the porch

name: Benjamin Reaches for a View, Queenie Pulls Him Back
description: Benjamin wheels his chair to the edge of the porch where the wall is lower, drawn by the sounds of children playing and carriages arriving on the street below. He leans forward, straining to see the activity beyond. Queenie suddenly grabs his wheelchair and pulls it back from the edge, rolling him away to the group of old people on the porch.
related_events: Benjamin wheels himself to the edge of the porch to see the street
Queenie pulls Benjamin's wheelchair back from the porch edge

name: Thomas nearly throws the baby into the water but pulls back
description: He comes along an old bridge over a waterway, the air heavy with the haze of fireworks, the water dark below. Thomas lifts the baby over the edge as if to drop it into the black water. At the apex of the motion, he stops. Instead of letting go, he pulls the newborn close, cradling it. 'I'm sorry... I'm so sorry...' he whispers. A lantern lights his face. A policeman down the way calls out, 'What are you doing there!?' The baby begins to cry. 'What do you have there?' the officer shouts. Thomas turns and runs, clutching the crying infant as the policeman starts after him.
related_events: Thomas lifts baby to throw into the water
Thomas decides against throwing the baby and cradles it instead
Thomas speaks apology to the baby

name: Lantern Light and the Policeman's Challenge
description: On the dark bridge, a lantern casts light on Thomas's face as he holds the crying baby. A policeman nearby calls out, 'What are you doing there!?' When the officer demands to know what Thomas is holding, Thomas turns and runs, clutching the baby as the policeman gives chase.
related_events: Lantern illuminates Thomas's face
Policeman confronts Thomas on the bridge

name: Thomas Runs with the Crying Baby
description: The baby begins to cry as the policeman calls out, demanding to know what Thomas is holding. Without responding, Thomas turns and runs, clutching the crying infant. The policeman starts chasing him down the dimly lit path beside the water.
related_events: Baby begins to cry
Thomas flees from the policeman while carrying the crying baby

name: Benjamin and Queenie Hold Hands and Talk
description: Benjamin lies on a bed on the floor near Queenie’s bed. He reaches out to hold her hand, and she gently takes it. They lie there together, hand in hand, through the quiet of the room. Benjamin says he feels different from the day before. Queenie tells him that everyone feels different in one way or another, that all people are moving the same way but take different roads. She says he is on his own road. Benjamin asks how much longer he has to live. Queenie replies that he should be thankful for what he has been given, that he has already lived longer than expected. The door opens quietly. Tizzy enters, looks at Benjamin, and signals for him to come. Benjamin gets up, and Tizzy carries him out, placing him in his wheelchair. Tizzy returns to the room, closes the door behind him, and stays with Queenie.
related_events: Benjamin reaches to hold Queenie's hand
Queenie takes Benjamin's hand
Benjamin expresses feeling different from the day before
Queenie offers philosophical reassurance about life's journey
Benjamin asks Queenie about how much longer he has to live

name: Tizzy Helps Benjamin into the Wheelchair for the Night
description: Tizzy opened the door quietly and stepped into the small room. Benjamin looked at him, then reached out as a signal to be picked up. Tizzy lifted him gently from the bed on the floor, carried him out of the room, and placed him into the wheelchair. He then returned to the room, moved to Queenie’s bedside, and stayed with her. Finally, he reached for the door and shut it quietly behind him.
related_events: Tizzy enters the room quietly
Benjamin signals Tizzy to pick him up
Tizzy carries Benjamin out of the room
Tizzy places Benjamin in his wheelchair
Tizzy returns to the room and stays with Queenie
Tizzy shuts the door quietly

name: Benjamin Hears Mr. Oti Under the Stairs
description: Benjamin lies on the floor near the stairs, playing with metal army men, when he hears Mr. Oti's laugh and voice drifting up from beneath the stairs. He reaches for his canes, gets up, and moves slowly toward the sound. As he approaches, he sees Mr. Oti standing in an alcove under the stairs with some of the other workers, speaking in a different tone, telling a story that draws laughter from the group. When Mr. Oti turns and notices Benjamin, Benjamin begins to retreat, using his canes to make his way quickly back up the stairs.
related_events: Benjamin hears Mr. Oti's voice from under the stairs
Benjamin uses his canes to go investigate the sound

name: Mr. Oti Tells His Story Under the Stairs
description: Benjamin lies on the floor near the stairs, playing with metal army men. From beneath the stairs, Mr. Oti’s laugh carries up, followed by his voice. Using his canes, Benjamin pulls himself up and moves toward the sound. Under the stairs, in a small alcove, Mr. Oti stands with members of the household staff, speaking in a sharp, mocking tone. He tells of being brought to St. Louis for the 1904 World's Fair, placed in a village of huts, made to live like they were in Africa while people stared from behind bars. He recalls being told not to look at the visitors, to act as if they were living their normal lives, and scoffs at the absurdity. The group laughs. Mr. Oti continues, describing how, when the day’s performance ended, they climbed over the walls at night and went to The Rosebud, where they drank and laughed freely until morning. As he speaks, he senses Benjamin’s presence. He turns. Benjamin, seeing he has been noticed, quickly retreats on his canes, moving back up the stairs.
related_events: Mr. Oti tells a satirical version of his life story to the household staff
Mr. Oti describes being exhibited at the 1904 World's Fair
Mr. Oti describes escaping the exhibit at night to visit The Rosebud

name: Benjamin Retreats Upstairs as Mr. Oti Turns
description: Benjamin lies on the floor near the stairs, playing with metal army men. The sound of Mr. Oti’s laugh rises from beneath the stairs, where he stands in an alcove with members of the household staff, speaking in a mocking tone about being brought to St. Louis for the 1904 World’s Fair, living in huts, performing as savages by day, then sneaking out at night to drink and laugh at The Rosebud. As Mr. Oti senses someone nearby, he stops and turns toward the stairs. Benjamin, seeing this, grabs his canes and moves quickly up the stairs, retreating out of sight.
related_events: Mr. Oti senses Benjamin's presence and turns
Benjamin retreats on his canes back up the stairs

name: Tizzy Confronts Queenie About the Baby
description: Tizzy Hambert knocks lightly on Queenie's door. She lies in bed, unable to sleep, gazing out a small window. He enters and tells her that the baby is not hers to keep, that it is not even of human kind. The baby cries out suddenly, then falls silent. Tizzy turns and begins to leave. Queenie whispers, 'Mr. Weathers. Stay with me tonight.' He slows, but does not respond. She adds softly, 'You never know what's comin' for you.' He continues toward the door as she remains still in the dim room.
related_events: Tizzy Hambert delivers message to Queenie
Baby cries out and then falls silent
Tizzy Hambert begins to leave after confrontation

name: Queenie Asks Mr. Weathers to Stay
description: Queenie lies in bed, unable to sleep, gazing out a small window. A light knock comes at the door. Tizzy speaks briefly, then leaves. The baby cries and falls silent. Queenie whispers, 'Mr. Weathers. Stay with me tonight.' He hesitates. She adds softly, 'You never know what's comin' for you.' They move together, beginning to make love. Nearby, a dresser drawer is open just a crack. Inside, Benjamin lies among the clothes, looking out.
related_events: Queenie lies awake and observes through window
Queenie whispers request to Mr. Weathers to stay
Queenie and Mr. Weathers begin to make love

name: Benjamin Watches from the Drawer
description: Benjamin lies hidden in a dresser drawer, slightly ajar, among folded clothes. He watches silently as Queenie and Mr. Weathers come together in the dim room. The baby stirs, then quiets. As they move toward each other, the drawer remains open just enough for him to see. In a soft voice, he says, 'I found a home.'
related_events: Benjamin observes from open dresser drawer
Benjamin reflects on finding a home

name: Queenie and Tizzy Serve Dinner
description: Queenie, in a white uniform, and Tizzy, wearing a chef's hat and apron, move through the dining area serving dinner to the boarders. The residents sit at the table, their faces lined with age, eating quietly. Benjamin Button sits among them in a wheelchair, small and hunched, his hands and legs twisted by arthritis. He wears eyeglasses and a hearing aid, and wisps of white hair grow faintly on his scalp. As he eats, he bangs his fork against the plate, making noise. Queenie steps over and adjusts the fork in his hand. 'Stop bangin' that fork... It's for eating, not for playin' with,' she says. 'And use your napkin, please Mr. Benjamin.' He obeys, wiping his mouth. Nearby, a staff member feeds one of the older men. Benjamin eats his meal like the others, just another elderly man at the dinner table.
related_events: Queenie and Tizzy serve dinner to the boarders
Benjamin Button sits at dinner among elderly boarders

name: Queenie Corrects Benjamin's Table Manners
description: Benjamin sits at the dinner table among the elderly boarders, his hands gnarled and stiff with age. He bangs his fork against the plate, making noise, the clatter cutting through the quiet dining room. Queenie, in her white uniform, turns to him and speaks firmly, 'Stop bangin' that fork... It's for eating, not for playin' with.' She adjusts the fork in his arthritic hand. 'And use your napkin, please Mr. Benjamin.' He obeys, wiping his mouth with the napkin. Nearby, a staff member feeds one of the other old men, while Benjamin, quiet now, continues his meal like the others.
related_events: Benjamin Button bangs his fork noisily during dinner
Queenie corrects Benjamin Button's table manners
Benjamin Button complies with Queenie's instructions

name: Benjamin's Hair Begins to Grow
description: Benjamin sits in a wheelchair among the elderly boarders during dinner, his hands and legs twisted with age. He wears eyeglasses and a hearing aid, and Queenie adjusts his fork, reminding him to eat properly and use his napkin. As he bangs the fork against his plate, she corrects him gently. Nearby, a staff member feeds one of the older men. Amid the routine, thin strands of white hair—faint but visible—begin to appear on Benjamin’s scalp, growing in where there had been none before.
related_events: Benjamin Button's hair begins to grow in as white wisps

name: Staff Member Feeds Elderly Boarder During Dinner
description: During dinner, a staff member approaches one of the elderly boarders and helps him eat, guiding food to his mouth with a spoon. The man sits quietly, dependent on the assistance, while others at the table continue their meals. Benjamin Button, seated in his wheelchair, watches or eats on his own, part of the same quiet routine.
related_events: A staff member feeds one of the elderly boarders

name: Benjamin Sees Ngunda Oti with the Elderly on the Lawn
description: Benjamin walks into the kitchen and stops, noticing a small African man with his back turned, standing on the lawn surrounded by a group of elderly people. The man speaks, telling them about being captured by a neighboring tribe of cannibals. One of the old women reacts in shock, asking if he escaped. He says he crossed the river, but his first wife could not swim and was eaten. Tizzy, busy preparing lunch, tells Benjamin the man is Mr. Oti, an acquaintance of an acquaintance, who will be staying in the staff quarters for a while. Mr. Oti continues his story, saying his second wife died after stepping on a viper, and the group laughs at his remark about it being bad luck to be married to him. He then says he was captured with six others by the Baschiele tribe and sold to a big white man.
related_events: Benjamin enters the kitchen and observes Ngunda Oti with the elderly group

name: Ngunda Oti Tells His Story on the Lawn
description: Benjamin walks into the kitchen and sees Tizzy preparing lunch. Outside, an elderly African man stands on the lawn surrounded by other old people. The man, Ngunda Oti, speaks of being captured by a neighboring tribe of cannibals. The group flinches at the word. He says he escaped by crossing the river, but his first wife could not swim and was eaten. An old woman stares wide-eyed and asks if he really survived the cannibals. He nods. Then, with a jocular tone, he tells them his second wife stepped on a viper and died. The old people laugh nervously. Tizzy explains to Benjamin that Mr. Oti is staying in the staff quarters. Oti continues, saying he was captured again, this time with six others, by the Baschiele tribe, who sold them to a big white man.
related_events: Ngunda Oti recounts capture by a cannibal tribe and escape across the river
Old people react with fear to mention of cannibals
Old woman expresses shock at Ngunda Oti's escape from cannibals
Ngunda Oti reveals death of second wife due to viper bite

name: Ngunda Oti Tells of Being Captured by the Baschiele and Sold to a White Man
description: Ngunda Oti stands on the lawn surrounded by old people, speaking calmly as they listen. He tells them that he was captured with six others by the Baschiele tribe. After the capture, they were sold to a big white man. The old people remain silent, absorbing his words as he recounts the event with quiet resolve.
related_events: Ngunda Oti describes capture by Baschiele tribe and sale to a white man

name: Queenie Presents Benjamin to the Old People
description: Queenie enters the parlor carrying a bundled baby. The Old People, who had been talking and playing cards, fall silent and turn to her. She tells them they have a visitor who will be staying for a while—her sister’s child, Benjamin. She explains that he is not well and will need their care. The group listens quietly as she speaks.
related_events: Queenie introduces Benjamin to the Old People
The Old People pause their activities to listen to Queenie

name: The Old Woman Takes the Baby
description: One of the women in the parlor says she has raised ten children and can care for any baby. She reaches out to hold Benjamin. Queenie hesitates, then passes the bundle into her arms. The woman pulls back the blanket covering the infant’s face and gasps, startled by what she sees.
related_events: Old Woman claims she can care for the baby due to her experience
Queenie reluctantly hands the baby to the Old Woman
Old Woman uncovers the baby's face and reacts in shock

name: Queenie Introduces Benjamin and the Group Reacts
description: Queenie brings a bundle into the parlor and tells the gathered people that her sister had a child who could not care for him, and that he will be staying with them. She names him Benjamin, testing the name with quiet approval. She explains that he is not well and that the doctor says he does not have much time. One of the old women, confident from experience, asks to hold the baby. After some hesitation, Queenie hands the child over. The woman pulls back the blanket from the baby’s face and exclaims that he looks just like her ex-husband, drawing laughter from the others. A man remarks, 'Join the club,' and the group laughs again. The baby, in response to the sound, seems to smile—a faint, lonely smile, like that of an old, dying man.
related_events: Queenie reveals the baby's premature aging and poor prognosis
Man responds to Queenie's revelation with dark humor
Group laughs after Old Woman's exclamation about the baby's resemblance
Baby appears to smile in response to the group's laughter

name: Tizzy Watches the Introduction with Disapproval
description: Queenie brings a baby bundle into the parlor and announces that her sister had a child who couldn't care for him, introducing him as Benjamin. She explains he is not well and will be staying with them. As the Old People stop their activities to listen, Tizzy comes out of the kitchen and stands nearby, watching the scene with a clear look of disapproval. One of the women, remarking that she had ten children and can handle any baby, reaches for the infant. Queenie hesitates but hands the baby over. The woman pulls back the blanket from the baby’s face and startles, exclaiming that he looks just like her ex-husband, drawing laughter from the group. Queenie adds that Benjamin is prematurely old and the doctor says he doesn’t have much time left. A man responds, 'Join the club,' prompting more laughter. The baby appears to smile, a faint, lonely smile like that of an old, dying man.
related_events: Tizzy emerges from the kitchen with visible disapproval

name: Doctor Rose Examines the Baby
description: Doctor Rose stands by Queenie's bed, stethoscope hanging at his side, and washes his hands in the sink. He looks at the baby lying in the bed, his expression grave. He speaks quietly, describing the infant’s clouded eyes, stiff joints, and hardened hands and feet. He says the baby is nearly blind, likely deaf, his body worn with the signs of advanced age. Queenie listens, then tells him the child is her sister’s from Lafayette, born after an unfortunate event. She whispers that the child came out white. Doctor Rose replies that there are places for babies like this, that they don’t have room here. Queenie insists the baby won’t last long. He pauses, then says some creatures aren’t meant to survive. She looks at the baby, her voice firm, calling him a miracle—just not the kind anyone hopes for.
related_events: Doctor Rose examines the Baby on Queenie's bed
Doctor Rose diagnoses the Baby with symptoms of extreme old age

name: Queenie and Doctor Rose Confront the Baby's Condition
description: Queenie lies the baby on her bed, watching as Doctor Rose washes his hands in the sink. He examines the infant, noting the cataracts, hearing loss, arthritic bones, and ossified hands and feet. He says the baby is dying of old age, his body failing before life has truly begun. Queenie asks if he means the child is dying, and Doctor Rose confirms it is from old age. He looks at the baby and then at Queenie, asking where the child came from. Queenie pauses before answering that he is her sister’s child from Lafayette, born after an unfortunate incident, and whispers that the child came out white. Doctor Rose replies that there are places for unwanted babies like this one, and that the Nolan Foundation already sees the household as a burden. Queenie pleads, reminding him the baby doesn’t have long. Doctor Rose tells her some creatures aren’t meant to survive. She looks at the baby, then says he is a miracle—just not the kind anyone hopes to see.
related_events: Doctor Rose questions the origin of the Baby

name: Queenie Reveals the Baby's Origin and Pleads for His Stay
description: Queenie tells Doctor Rose that the baby is her sister's child from Lafayette, born after a tragic incident. She explains that the child came out white and has been left in her care. Doctor Rose expresses concern about the burden of another mouth to feed and suggests taking the baby to a home for unwanted children. Queenie, looking at the infant, says he doesn’t have long to live. She insists he is a miracle, though not the kind anyone hopes for, and pleads for him to be allowed to stay.
related_events: Queenie reveals the Baby's origin as her sister's child from Lafayette
Queenie appeals to Doctor Rose by referencing the Baby's short life expectancy

name: Queenie and Doctor Rose Argue Over the Baby's Future
description: Doctor Rose stands by the sink, drying his hands after washing them, his stethoscope hanging at his neck. He looks at the baby lying on Queenie's bed, its body frail and aged in appearance. The doctor speaks plainly, saying the child is nearly blind, barely able to hear, his bones stiff with arthritis, his skin lifeless, his hands and feet hardened. He says the baby is dying of old age, that his body is failing before life has truly begun. Queenie asks if the baby is dying. The doctor confirms it, adding that the child cannot survive. He suggests sending the baby to an institution, pointing out there is no room for another mouth to feed, especially with the Nolan Foundation already viewing the place as a burden. Queenie hesitates, then says the baby is her sister's child from Lafayette, born after an unfortunate incident, and whispers that the child came out white. The doctor insists such babies are better off in care facilities. Queenie looks at the infant, then back at the doctor, and says the baby is a miracle—just not the kind people hope for.
related_events: Doctor Rose suggests placing the Baby in an institution
Doctor Rose expresses fatalistic view on the Baby's survival
Queenie declares the Baby a miracle despite its condition

name: Caroline Sits with Her Mother and Shares Her Regrets
description: Caroline sits on the bed beside her dying mother, Daisy. The wind rattles the window. She tells Daisy she hopes she hasn’t disappointed her. Daisy replies that she could never be disappointed. Caroline says she wished she had more to show for her life, that she knows Daisy would have liked grandchildren, and that her life hasn’t been normal—like the pieces never quite fit. She says she’s always either a step ahead or a step behind. Daisy asks what normal is, then says, “A hat full of sand.”
related_events: Caroline expresses regret about her life to her dying mother
Daisy compares normalcy to a hat full of sand

name: Dorothy Baker Asks to Call Her Son
description: The wind rattles the window as Dorothy Baker turns to Caroline and asks if she can make a phone call. She explains that she has someone watching her little boy and would like to check in on him. Caroline tells her to go ahead, and Dorothy leaves the room to make the call, while the quiet settles back around Caroline and her mother.
related_events: Dorothy Baker requests permission to make a phone call

name: Caroline Reads Benjamin's Journal to Daisy
description: Caroline opens a suitcase by the bed and finds an old envelope among clothes and keepsakes. She takes it out and sees a collection of handwritten pages, loose sheets, and scraps of paper, some written on napkins. Daisy, lying in bed, asks her to read it aloud. Caroline begins reading from the papers, her voice quiet, starting with the date 'April 4, 1985' and the words 'New Orleans.' As she reads, Daisy closes her eyes, listening.
related_events: Caroline retrieves an old envelope from Daisy's suitcase
Daisy asks Caroline to read from the journal

name: Caroline Reads Benjamin's Journal to Daisy
description: Caroline sits beside her mother on the bed and begins reading aloud from an old envelope filled with handwritten pages, scraps of paper, and napkins. The first entry is dated April 4, 1985, from New Orleans. She reads Benjamin Button’s words: 'This is my last will and testament... I don't have much to leave... few possessions, no money really... I will go out of this world the same way I came in, alone and with nothing. All I have is my story... I'm writing it now while I still remember it.' She pauses and looks over at Daisy, who has her eyes closed. Caroline continues, 'My name is Benjamin... Benjamin Button... and I was born under unusual circumstances,' reading steadily, her voice filling the quiet room as the wind rattles the window.
related_events: Caroline begins reading Benjamin's journal aloud
Benjamin introduces himself in his journal
Caroline observes her mother's reaction while reading

name: Mr. Cake Unveils the Clock
description: Mr. Cake, aided by an assistant, climbs the scaffolding to the covered clock. Below, a crowd gathers, watching in anticipation. Among them stands Theodore Roosevelt, dressed in overcoat and hat, his presence solemn. Mr. Cake reaches the top, positions himself before the draped clock, and prepares to pull the cord.
related_events: Mr. Cake climbs scaffolding to unveil the clock
Theodore Roosevelt arrives at the clock unveiling

name: Mr. Cake Unveils the Clock
description: Mr. Cake, standing on the scaffolding with an assistant beside him, grasps the cord attached to the purple velvet drape covering the clock. He gives it a firm tug. The drape falls away, revealing the clock in its full splendor. Below, the crowd lets out a collective gasp, their eyes fixed on the gleaming timepiece.
related_events: Mr. Cake pulls the cord to reveal the clock
Crowd gasps at the sight of the unveiled clock

name: Mr. Cake Activates the Clock
description: After the velvet drape falls away, Mr. Cake steps forward and winds the clock mechanism. The clock chimes for the first time, a clear and resonant sound that fills the square. Above the face, a small angel figure seems to push the second hand into motion as it begins its first rotation. The crowd breaks into cheers, clapping and smiling as the clock starts ticking.
related_events: Mr. Cake winds the clock mechanism
Clock chimes for the first time
Second hand begins moving, pushed by angel figure
Crowd cheers after the clock starts

name: The Clock That Ran Backwards
description: The crowd gathered for the unveiling watched as Mr. Cake pulled away the velvet drape covering the clock. With a tug, the purple cloth fell, revealing the gleaming timepiece. He wound it, and the clock chimed, rich and clear. The second hand, pushed as if by an unseen force, began to move—slowly at first, then steadily—counterclockwise. Murmurs spread through the onlookers. A man near the front called out, 'It's running backwards!' The words rippled through the crowd. Monsieur Gateau stepped forward, his voice calm. 'I made it this way,' he said, 'so that perhaps, the boys who were lost in the war might stand and go home again.'
related_events: Crowd realizes the clock is moving backwards in time
Man shouts that the clock is running backwards
Monsieur Gateau reveals he designed the clock to run backwards

name: Queenie Defends Her Daughter Against Mrs. Duprey
description: A woman's voice calls out, saying Queenie's daughter has soiled herself again. Queenie, tending to the baby, tells Jane Childress to start the bath and snaps at Mrs. Duprey to mind her own business, adding that Mrs. Duprey will be soiling herself soon enough. She soothes the baby quietly, then opens a dresser drawer to find a place to put it.
related_events: Mrs. Duprey comments on Queenie's daughter soiling herself
Queenie responds defiantly to Mrs. Duprey's comment

name: Queenie Reassures Mrs. Hollister About Her Necklace
description: There is a knock on Queenie's door. Mrs. Hollister enters, whispering that someone stole her necklace. Queenie gently tells her the pearls are right there, around her neck, and guides her with a soft touch. Mrs. Hollister calms, and Queenie turns her attention toward the door as a chime sounds in the distance.
related_events: Someone knocks on Queenie's door
Mrs. Hollister reports her necklace has been stolen
Queenie reassures Mrs. Hollister about the missing necklace

name: Queenie Soothes the Baby and Answers Apple's Call
description: Queenie whispers to the baby, calming it with soft words. She opens a dresser drawer, places the baby inside among her undergarments, and closes the drawer just enough to leave a small opening. As she turns to leave, she hears a voice calling—Apple will not take a bath without her. Queenie replies, 'Mercy, I'll be right there,' and moves toward the door.
related_events: Queenie soothes the baby with whispered words
Queenie places the baby in a dresser drawer
Apple refuses to take a bath without Queenie

name: Queenie Responds to Dr. Rose's Arrival
description: A door chime sounds. A woman's voice announces that Dr. Rose has arrived for his visit. Queenie turns, glancing back toward the dresser drawer where the baby lies hidden among her underclothes, the lilac sachet scent lingering in the air. The baby, with the face of an old man, looks up through the narrow opening at the sliver of light. Queenie closes the door behind her and leaves the room.
related_events: Dr. Rose arrives for his visit
Queenie checks on the Baby before leaving the room

name: The Baby in the Drawer
description: Inside the dresser drawer, among unmentionables and the scent of a lilac sachet, the Baby lies with the face of an old man, staring up at the narrow slit of light filtering through the slightly ajar drawer.
related_events: The Baby appears with the face of an old man inside the dresser drawer

name: Oti Questions Benjamin's Age and Identity
description: Mr. Oti appears suddenly and sits down across from Benjamin, who is reading at the dining table. Oti teases him, saying he doesn’t look as old as he seems and asks if he’s fooling everyone, wondering aloud whether Benjamin has Madjembe. Benjamin, confused, asks what Madjembe is. Oti replies, 'Worms.' Benjamin insists he is not pretending and is not afflicted.
related_events: Mr. Oti appears and sits across from Benjamin
Mr. Oti teases Benjamin about his appearance
Benjamin asks about meaning of madjembe
Mr. Oti explains madjembe as worms
Benjamin denies pretending or being afflicted

name: Mr. Oti Invites Benjamin for Root Beer
description: Mr. Oti looks away from Benjamin and toward the street, then casually suggests they go get a cold root beer. Benjamin responds that it's dangerous, but Mr. Oti asks who said that, his tone questioning and light. Mr. Oti stands up and, looking back at Benjamin, says, 'Come on little man...' Benjamin hesitates, glancing toward Queenie, who leans out of a window and beats dust from a rug. After a moment, he takes up his canes, rises, and follows Mr. Oti outside. The door closes behind them.
related_events: Mr. Oti suggests getting a cold root beer
Benjamin expresses concern about danger
Mr. Oti challenges Benjamin's warning
Mr. Oti urges Benjamin to come along

name: Benjamin Follows Mr. Oti Outside
description: Benjamin sits at the dining room table, his attention drawn to Queenie as she leans out of a window, beating dust from a rug. Mr. Oti rises and moves toward the door, glancing back. Benjamin reaches for his canes, stands, and follows. The door closes behind them.
related_events: Benjamin observes Queenie beating dust from a rug
Benjamin decides to follow Mr. Oti outside
Benjamin steps into the unknown
The door closes behind Benjamin and Mr. Oti

name: Tizzy Corrects Benjamin's Misreading
description: Tizzy washes dishes while Benjamin puts away cans, reading aloud from a label. Benjamin says 'myasses' and Tizzy swats him with a dish towel, correcting him: 'Molasses.'
related_events: Benjamin reads ingredients from a can label
Tizzy corrects Benjamin's misreading of molasses

name: Tizzy Recalls Learning to Read and Recites Shakespeare
description: Tizzy washes dishes beside Benjamin, who puts away cans and reads from a label. 'Tomato, brown sugar, salt, myasses,' Benjamin says. Tizzy swats him with a dish towel. 'Molasses,' he corrects. As he continues washing, Tizzy says he learned to read at five. His grandfather, a dresser for a famous actor, brought home plays for him. He recites a passage from Shakespeare: 'Kind keepers of my weak decaying age, Let dying Mortimer here rest himself. Even like a man new haled from the rack, So fare my limbs with long imprisonment. And these gray locks, the pursuivants of death, Nestor-like aged in an age of care, Argue the end of Edmund Mortimer.' Benjamin stares, stunned. Tizzy asks if he thought him ignorant. Before Benjamin can answer, an old man appears in the doorway. 'When's dessert?' he asks. 'When it's served,' Tizzy replies. 'Now sit your wrinkly butt back down, Mr. Lee.'
related_events: Tizzy shares story about learning to read at age five
Tizzy recites a passage from Shakespeare's play

name: Tizzy Corrects Benjamin's Misunderstanding
description: Tizzy washes dishes while Benjamin puts away cans, reading from a label. He says 'myasses' and Tizzy swats him with a dish towel, correcting him: 'Molasses.' As he continues washing, Tizzy says he learned to read at five. His grandfather, a dresser for a famous actor, brought home plays for him—Shakespeare. He recites a passage from memory: 'Kind keepers of my weak decaying age, let dying Mortimer here rest himself...' Benjamin listens, stunned. Tizzy asks if he thought he was ignorant. Before Benjamin can answer, an old man appears in the doorway and asks when dessert will be served. Tizzy tells him to sit back down, it will be served when it's ready.
related_events: Tizzy confronts Benjamin about assuming her ignorance
Tizzy reveals her grandfather worked for John Wilkes Booth

name: Benjamin Witnesses Tizzy's Recitation
description: Benjamin stands beside Tizzy as he washes dishes, listening in silence. Tizzy recites lines from a Shakespeare play, his voice steady and full of presence. When he finishes, he tells Benjamin about learning to read at five, about his grandfather who worked for a famous actor—John Wilkes Booth. Benjamin’s mouth hangs open, his expression fixed in quiet amazement. An old man pokes his head in and asks about dessert. Tizzy tells him to sit back down. Benjamin remains still, staring at Tizzy, as the moment lingers.
related_events: Benjamin reacts with awe to Tizzy's recitation

name: Tizzy and the Dessert Interruption
description: An old man peered in and asked when dessert would be served, cutting into Tizzy's story. Tizzy turned and told him, 'When it's served. Now sit your wrinkly butt back down, Mr. Lee.' The man retreated, and the moment settled again.
related_events: Man interrupts Tizzy to ask about dessert
Tizzy tells Mr. Lee to sit back down

name: Benjamin Remembers Church on Saturday Nights
description: Benjamin, speaking in voiceover, recalls how he used to go to Queenie's church on Saturday nights.
related_events: Benjamin recalls attending Queenie's church on Saturday nights

name: Thomas Button Bids Farewell to His Dying Wife
description: Thomas Button enters the bedroom where his wife lies pale and trembling, surrounded by the doctor and household staff. The doctor turns to him and says, 'Thomas, I'm afraid she's not going to survive.' Thomas moves to the bed, kneels beside her, and takes her hand. He tells her he came as quickly as he could, apologizing for the delay because the streets were filled with people. She looks at him with fearful eyes, pleading, 'Promise me, Thomas...' and clutches his hand tightly. Before she can finish, her voice fades, her grip loosens, and she stops breathing. The doctor checks her pulse, then silently covers her body. The priest begins murmuring prayers, and the maids weep quietly in the room.
related_events: Doctor informs Thomas Button of his wife's critical condition
Thomas Button kneels beside his wife and takes her hand
Thomas Button apologizes for delayed arrival due to crowded streets
Wife pleads for a promise from Thomas Button
Wife utters final plea and dies clutching Thomas Button's hand

name: The Aftermath of the Wife's Death
description: The doctor checks the woman’s pulse, then silently draws the sheet over her body. The priest leans close, murmuring words under his breath as the housemaids cry, their faces wet with tears. Thomas stays on his knees beside the bed, gripping his wife’s hand, his body motionless. A soft voice speaks, saying she gave her life for him, and he is forever grateful. The room is quiet except for the hushed prayers and weeping.
related_events: Doctor confirms wife's death and covers her body
Priest murmurs incantations over the deceased wife
Housemaids weep at the wife's death
Thomas Button remains kneeling, unable to let go of his wife's hand
Benjamin Button's voiceover expresses gratitude for his mother's sacrifice

name: The Baby's Unnatural Cry
description: A sudden cry broke the silence in the room. The newborn’s wail was deep and haunting, unlike the cry of any healthy infant. Everyone froze, turning toward the sound. The maids stopped weeping, the priest paused his murmurs, and Thomas lifted his head from beside his wife’s body. Benjamin Button’s voice spoke softly, saying she had given her life for him, and for that he would always be grateful. The room remained still, all eyes now on the swaddled baby in the basket, its face hidden beneath cloth.
related_events: Newborn baby cries suddenly during bedside scene
Newborn baby emits unnatural, haunting wail
All present fall silent and turn toward the baby's cry
Benjamin Button's voiceover expresses gratitude for his mother's sacrifice

name: Thomas Discovers the Infant's Face and Flees
description: Thomas turned toward the swaddled baby as it let out a deep, unnatural wail. A maid called out, 'Mr. Button...!' but he moved forward, lifting the cloth that covered the infant's face. His breath caught; his body stiffened, then recoiled in shock. A soft, horrified 'Ohhhh' escaped him. In one motion, he seized the bundled child and rushed from the room, descending the stairs and running out into the night.
related_events: Thomas Button approaches the swaddled baby despite maid's warning
Thomas Button recoils in horror and flees with the swaddled infant

name: Thomas Leaves the Baby on the Porch
description: Thomas arrives at an old three-story house with a screened porch, the sound of voices and laughter spilling from inside. The baby, calmed by the soft yellow light and the murmur of conversation, stops crying. Thomas sets the infant down on the back porch steps, then takes out all the money he has and tucks it into the blanket. He knocks on the weathered screen door and, without waiting, turns and walks away, leaving the baby behind.
related_events: Thomas leaves his baby on the back porch of a house
Thomas tucks money into the baby's blanket
Thomas knocks on the weathered screen door

name: Queenie and Tizzy on the Porch
description: Queenie steps onto the back porch in her green dress, followed by Tizzy. The air is still, the night quiet. Tizzy tells her she looks handsome, says the green matches her eyes. She runs a finger along the fabric, says it isn’t every day a war ends, they have to mark it somehow. He tips his hat, smiles. He tells her Hambert is back in town, came home without his legs. She pauses, then says she was sweeter on him than she should have been. When he asks if she knew about the legs, she answers, 'You never know what's comin' for you.' Inside, an older woman calls out—Ms. Simone has messed herself again. Queenie sighs, says she’ll be right there. But she lingers, says it’s nice out here. Tizzy agrees, says she should come out back for a moment, take her mind off things. He pushes the screen door open, offers his hand. She takes it. They step onto the porch together when suddenly Tizzy stumbles, nearly falls. Something is on the steps. Queenie moves closer, pulls back the blanket, and freezes. A baby lies there, wailing—a newborn with the face of an old man, wrinkled and pale-eyed. She whispers, 'God in heaven.' Tizzy says it looks like a milk wagon ran over it. He didn’t see it, hopes he didn’t hurt it. Queenie stares, then suddenly picks the baby up and carries it inside. Tizzy follows, whispering, close behind.
related_events: Tizzy compliments Queenie's appearance
Queenie reflects on the end of the war
Tizzy announces Hambert's return from war
Queenie expresses sorrow over Hambert's lost legs
Tizzy proposes a party for Hambert

name: Queenie Attends to Ms. Simone's Accident
description: An older white woman, Mrs. Jameson, steps out onto the porch and interrupts the conversation between Queenie and Tizzy. She tells Queenie that Ms. Simone has soiled herself. Queenie sighs, expressing frustration, and says Ms. Simone will have to wear diapers if she keeps doing it. She tells Mrs. Jameson she’ll be right there, but lingers on the porch, clearly not eager to go back inside.
related_events: Mrs. Jameson reports that Ms. Simone soiled herself
Queenie responds to Ms. Simone's accident

name: Tizzy and Queenie Find the Baby on the Porch
description: Tizzy pushes open the screen door and invites Queenie to step out back, offering her his hand. She takes it, smiling, and he backs out onto the porch. As he steps down, he suddenly stumbles, nearly falling, and a baby wails beneath his foot. Queenie moves toward the sound, pushes aside the blanket, and freezes. The baby has the bald head of a newborn, but its face is wrinkled and aged, with the sunken eyes and sagging skin of an old man. She gasps, murmuring in disbelief. Tizzy, shaken, says he didn’t see it there and worries he hurt the child. The baby continues to cry. After a moment, Queenie reaches down, picks up the infant, and carries it inside. Tizzy follows close behind.
related_events: Tizzy invites Queenie to come out back
Tizzy steps on the baby by accident
Queenie discovers the baby's unusual appearance

name: Queenie Takes the Baby Inside
description: After stepping on the baby and stumbling back in shock, Tizzy stares at the wailing infant, muttering that he hopes he didn’t hurt it. He suggests they leave it for the police. Queenie crouches down, looking at the child wrapped in the blanket, its old, wrinkled face contrasting with its tiny body. She says softly that no one wanted to keep it. Without another word, she reaches down, picks up the crying baby, and turns toward the house. Tizzy hesitates, whispering something under his breath, then follows her through the screen door.
related_events: Tizzy expresses concern about harming the baby
Queenie decides to take the baby inside
Tizzy follows Queenie into the house with the baby

name: Daisy's Final Hours
description: Daisy Fuller lies in a hospital bed, her voice faint as she murmurs about memories that slip through her grasp, speaking of a train station and a tuba band playing oom-pah-pah. Her blue eyes drift out the window, unfocused, as she complains of a mouth full of cotton and the sensation of drifting on a boat. She grows restless, scratching at her nightgown until it bunches and irritates her skin. Dorothy Baker, the caregiver, watches from the corner before stepping forward to smooth the fabric and gently restrain her. Daisy winces with each breath, the pain coming more frequently. Dorothy adjusts the morphine drip, and Daisy closes her eyes, her body slowly sinking into the drug’s haze. The room grows quiet except for the soft sounds of labored breathing.
related_events: Daisy Fuller reflects on fragmented memories while nearing death
Dorothy Baker intervenes as Daisy attempts to remove her nightgown
Daisy experiences increasing physical pain and discomfort

name: Dorothy Baker Tells Caroline That Daisy Is Dying
description: Dorothy Baker, the caregiver, watches Daisy Fuller closely as she stirs restlessly in bed, scratching at her nightgown. After gently straightening the fabric, Dorothy turns to Caroline and says quietly, 'It’s their way of letting go… prob’ly today.' Caroline looks at her mother, silent and pale in the hospital bed, and nods, understanding the weight of the words. The room grows heavier, the air still, as the reality of Daisy’s condition settles between them.
related_events: Dorothy Baker informs Caroline about Daisy's imminent passing

name: Caroline Says Goodbye to Her Mother Daisy
description: Caroline sits beside her mother Daisy’s bed in the hospital room, asking if she wants more medication. Daisy does not answer, her eyes fixed on some distant point. Caroline begins to cry, overwhelmed, and thanks her mother for bringing her into the world and raising her with care. She tells Daisy how much she means to her and how deeply she will be missed. Daisy, weak and fading, lifts her thin arms to embrace her daughter, holding her gently. They remain together in silence, the weight of the moment settling between them.
related_events: Caroline offers comfort and medication to her dying mother Daisy
Caroline expresses gratitude and love to her dying mother Daisy
Daisy comforts Caroline during her emotional breakdown

name: Caroline Asks If Daisy Is Afraid
description: After holding each other in a long embrace, Caroline and Daisy slowly pull apart. They sit in silence, the space between them filled with unspoken words. Caroline looks at her mother and asks, 'Are you afraid?' Daisy, her voice soft but clear, replies, 'Curious. What comes next.' She winces slightly, then closes her eyes as the morphine takes hold, her breath growing shallow.
related_events: Caroline and Daisy share a prolonged embrace followed by emotional silence
Caroline asks Daisy if she is afraid of dying
Daisy expresses curiosity about what comes after death

name: Dorothy Increases the Morphine
description: Dorothy Baker notices that Daisy's pain is coming more frequently and that her breathing will soon falter. She adjusts the morphine drip to ease Daisy's discomfort. The room grows quiet as Daisy closes her eyes, her body relaxing into a dream-like state. A soft murmur escapes her lips about a train station and a tuba band playing oom-pah-pah, her voice faint, drifting.
related_events: Dorothy Baker increases the morphine dosage to alleviate Daisy's suffering

name: Daisy Remembers the Train Station
description: Under the effects of the morphine, Daisy's eyes close and her breathing slows. A soft expression crosses her face as she speaks, her voice faint and distant. She recalls a train station being built, and her father there on the opening day. A tuba band plays, she says, humming a tune—'Oom-pah-pah'—as if hearing it once more. The words drift out like a fragment carried on the air, then she falls silent, her breath shallow, her body still.
related_events: Daisy recalls a memory of her husband at the opening of a train station

name: The Preacher Heals Queenie's Womb
description: Inside a sweltering Negro gospel tent, the preacher turns to Queenie and asks what ails her. She whispers to him, and he announces to the crowd that her insides are twisted, preventing her from bearing children. He places his hand on her stomach and cries out to the Lord, asking for forgiveness of her sins so she may conceive. With force, he presses into her abdomen, shouting, 'Out, damnable affliction!' The pressure nearly makes her collapse, but a nurse in a crisp white uniform steadies her. After she regains her balance, the preacher moves on to the next case.
related_events: Preacher inquires about Queenie's condition

name: The Preacher Confronts the Devil in Benjamin
description: The preacher turns to Benjamin in his wheelchair and asks about his condition. Queenie whispers that the devil is on his back, trying to ride him into the grave. The preacher places his hands on Benjamin, shouts at the demons 'Zebuchar' and 'Beelzebub,' and commands them to leave his body.

Preacher commands demons to leave Benjamin

name: Benjamin Reveals His Age at the Revival
description: The preacher turns to Benjamin in his wheelchair and asks how old he is. Benjamin looks up and says, 'I'm seven, but I look a lot older.' The preacher throws his head back and laughs, then calls out to the crowd, 'God bless you. He's seven!' The congregation bursts into laughter and applause. The preacher places his hands on Benjamin's shoulders and says that this is a man with optimism in his heart and belief in his soul, declaring that everyone is a child in the eyes of God.
related_events: Benjamin reveals his true age
Preacher declares Benjamin a man of optimism and faith

name: The Preacher Commands Benjamin to Rise
description: The preacher placed his hands on Benjamin's shoulders and shouted, 'In the name of God's glory, rise up!' Benjamin strained, his legs trembling beneath him, but slowly pulled himself to his feet. The congregation broke into applause as he stood, unsteady but upright, in the sweltering gospel tent.

Benjamin stands from his wheelchair

name: Benjamin Rises After Falling at the Revival
description: After taking two unsteady steps, Benjamin's arthritic legs buckle and he collapses to the floor. The aides in white nurse's uniforms move toward him, but the preacher raises his hand and stops them. He kneels beside Benjamin and urges him to rise, calling out for him to rise up like Lazarus. When Benjamin remains on the ground, the preacher stands over him and shouts the command again. Slowly, Benjamin begins to push himself up, lifting his body with effort until he is back on his feet.

name: Benjamin's Walk of Faith Across the Tent
description: The preacher told Benjamin to rise and walk, shouting for him to say hallelujah. He declared that Benjamin would walk by faith alone, without crutch or cane. With the preacher at his side, moving in step as if dancing, Benjamin began to hobble forward, one unsteady step at a time. Queenie came alongside, urging him on. The congregation called out in support, their voices rising with each step. Slowly, painfully, Benjamin made his way across the stage, reaching the far end, where the crowd erupted in loud 'Amens.'

name: The Preacher's Fall at the Gospel Tent Revival
description: At the height of the revival meeting, the preacher raised his arms high, shouting praises to the Lord, his voice thundering through the tent. Sweat poured down his face as he danced and preached with fiery intensity. Suddenly, he clutched his chest, his eyes widening in silence. He staggered, then collapsed straight to the ground. The crowd gasped. Nurses in crisp white uniforms rushed forward, kneeling beside his still body, checking for signs of life. Meanwhile, Benjamin stood frozen in his wheelchair, his face twisted in confusion, looking around at the commotion with no one to guide him.
